  "partial_result": "I found one mechanism worth funding, but only if a cheap test passes first. I can't claim the bottleneck is established: the evidence points at it without isolating it. Everything was read-only: no edits, no GPU or training jobs, no operator contact. I also used one background agent to summarise the 39 closed-lane docs.\n\n## Bottleneck: product identity is entangled with the photo's context\n\nIn-Shop labels say \"these images are the same product.\" They never say which pixels are the product. Within one product, the context (the fashion model, the rest of the outfit, pose, framing, studio) is nearly constant across its views. Any label-only objective can therefore fit the training products using context plus garment together. On unseen products, context then produces impostors that share a layout, pose or shoot with the query.\n\n**Evidence for:**\n- **Label-only changes are all null.** Every objective, readout, width, source and teacher change on the same images and labels failed. The fit set is already solved (99.36% R@1).\n- **More products helps.** Doubling the number of fit products gave +0.365pp, CI [0.154, 0.574], below your floor but real. More products means more context variation per garment.\n- **Same-pose impostors are enriched among misses.** Stratified odds ratio 1.73, CI [1.23, 2.43].\n- **Framing matters.** Misses are 1.78\u00d7 more likely when the gallery has no image with the same framing.\n- **The garment is a minority of the image.** I measured this from the committed crop-support receipt (512 fit images, all 256\u00d7256). The garment box has median area 26.6% of the image (10th\u201390th percentile 8.5%\u201356.7%) and touches a median 84 of 256 patches.\n\n**Evidence against:**\n- Misses without a same-shoot gallery image are only 6.6% of misses.\n- **Garment area doesn't track miss rate by pose.** Side views have a small garment (median 16% of area) but the lowest miss rate (1.05%). Full-body views are similar in area (12.6%) and miss at 3.18%.\n- **The garment-box crop result is weaker than it looks.** Cropping misses to the garment box flipped 86/151 of them. A crude colour histogram flipped 55.6% of the same misses, and that test had no sham, so it is not causal evidence.\n- **Two ideas I killed myself from the receipt:**\n  - \"Token dilution\" (small garment share causes misses) fails on the pose data above.\n  - \"Trim the white padding and spend those tokens on content\" has no premise: garment boxes reach both image borders.\n\n## Mechanism: context-swap training intervention\n\nDuring In-Shop training only, with a fixed probability p=0.5 per sample, keep the pixels inside the product's garment box. Replace every pixel outside the box with the same coordinates from an image of a **different** fit product, preferring the same filename pose. The label stays the product's. The swap happens before the existing crop and flip. Serving is untouched: full image, same encoder, head, 130-byte code and scorer.\n\n**Why it is causally different from the closed lanes:**\n- It is the only lane that cuts the link between context and label while holding the garment evidence fixed.\n- The garment-box crop needed boxes at test time, stripped context from every image, and was only a zero-training rescore of misses.\n- Wider crops vary framing but keep the product's own context.\n- The pose, acquisition, impostor and positive-tail arms reweight losses over the same entangled labels.\n- Captions, teachers and sources add outside information instead.\n- The new information here is the TRAIN garment-box annotation, used as an intervention rather than as an input.\n\n**Smallest source change:**\n- `ImageRows` (`scripts/train_sop_siglip2_compact.py:137`) accepts an optional `(row, donor_row)` index plus boxes, and pastes before augmentation. Plain integer indices behave exactly as today, so SOP is unchanged.\n- At `scripts/train_inshop_siglip2_unseen_gallery.py:912`, precompute a donor table from the fixed schedule, with choices keyed by SHA so the torch augmentation RNG isn't consumed.\n- Add a flag `--context-donor {sham,treatment}`.\n- Reuse the `boxed_image` box conversion the bbox and crop-retention probes already use.\n- The bank refresh stays as is.\n\n**Deployed information and cost:**\n- **Deployed code:** still 128 dimensions and 130 bytes. What changes is how those dimensions are split between context and garment evidence.\n- **Serving:** the executable is identical, so latency is unchanged by construction. Don't re-claim latency; reuse the existing exact serving harness only if this is ever promoted.\n- **Training:** about 0.5 extra JPEG decodes plus a paste per sample on CPU workers. GPU work and memory are unchanged.\n- **Limits:** In-Shop only, because SOP has no boxes. Using box annotations is extra supervision and must be disclosed when comparing to published results.\n\n**Prior art (cited from memory, not re-fetched):** there is no principled novelty here; it is a known intervention applied to garment context in In-Shop.\n- Tian et al., CVPR 2018, \"Eliminating Background-bias for Robust Person Re-identification\": random background replacement using person masks.\n- Xiao et al., ICLR 2021, arXiv:2006.09994: backgrounds taken from the same class versus a random class. This is the origin of the sham/treatment design below.\n- Dwibedi et al., ICCV 2017, arXiv:1708.01642; Ghiasi et al., CVPR 2021, arXiv:2012.07177 (cut/copy-paste augmentation).\n- Geirhos et al., 2020, arXiv:2004.07780 (shortcut learning).\n- Liu et al., CVPR 2016 (DeepFashion, the source of the box annotations).\n\n## F0: \u2264120 s TRAIN-fit falsifier (no training, no held read)\n\n- **Model:** the pinned seed-179026 true-freeze 1,000-update checkpoint (training receipt `76f1293a\u2026`).\n- **Gallery:** 768 fit products with at least two images, chosen by SHA order. All their native images (about 5,100) form the gallery.\n- **Queries:** one query per product, in three variants that share the same box geometry:\n  - **N:** the native image.\n  - **S (sham):** outside-box pixels from another image of the **same** product.\n  - **D (treatment):** outside-box pixels from a **different** selected product.\n- **Scoring:** exclude the query itself and the donor image. Report R@1 for N, S and D, plus how often D's top-1 lands on the donor product.\n- **Cost:** about 6,600 encodes at the measured ~188 images/s, roughly 35 s plus model load.\n\n**Kill rules** (funding floors, not proofs):\n- **KILL if S minus D is under 2.0pp, or its product-bootstrap 95% lower bound is \u22640.** The trained code doesn't use foreign context, so there is nothing to intervene on.\n- **KILL if N minus S is over 5.0pp.** The pasting artefacts alone are corrupting the input, so any effect couldn't be attributed.\n\n## If F0 passes\n\n- **What it licenses:** only the 17-update smoke. It shows the model relies on context, not that removing that reliance helps: context is also a legitimate cross-view cue for true positives.\n- **17-update smoke (seed 179024, freeze_emb, three arms: control / sham / treatment, run serially):**\n  - Schedule, labels and first-ten label hashes are identical across arms.\n  - Sham and treatment composite exactly the same samples.\n  - All updates finite with no skipped steps; frozen tensors equal the pretrained ones.\n  - Wall \u22641.10\u00d7 and peak CUDA \u22641.005\u00d7 control.\n- **Frozen 100-update gate (same three arms, fixed 6,354-query/6,245-gallery roles, packed scorer):**\n  - Primary: treatment minus sham mAP@R has product-bootstrap lower bound >0. This attributes any gain to the swap rather than to pasting as augmentation.\n  - Also required: treatment minus control point estimates for R@1 and mAP@R are \u22650 (report CIs), and cost guards hold.\n  - Descriptive only: same-pose-impostor misses and per-pose miss rates.\n  - A negative result closes this lane. It is not evidence about the pixels themselves.\n- **Paired-seed gate:** 1,000 updates on seeds 179025 and 179027, all three arms.\n  - Reuse archived controls only if byte-identical.\n  - Pass requires pooled treatment minus control R@1 lower bound >0, each seed's point estimate \u22650, and pooled treatment minus sham lower bound >0.\n  - A pass would permit one frozen, exploratory official read (TEST has already been observed). No SOTA claim, and no change to SOP or defaults.",

Every loss, proxy, freeze, LR, width, depth, crop, caption, and warm-start arm moved R@1 within noise while mAP moved.\n- The tokens still hold the answer: garment-box crop at inference rescues 86/151 miss triples (57%) with the unchanged checkpoint; raw tokens 53/151; source cosine to impostor max 0.96 (no duplicates). So the pooled 1024-D vector, not the 128-D head or int8 (float vs packed +0.03), is where garment detail is lost.\n- Impostor scaling is sublinear (65 misses at 1/4 products), pose enrichment 1.7\u20132.1\u00d7, framing twin 1.78\u00d7: template (model/pose/framing) content competes with garment content in the pooled vector.\n\n**What I cannot say from evidence:** whether the 57% crop rescue comes from removing model/background tokens or from *scale/position normalization* of the garment. Every lane closed so far (bbox attention, wider random crop, quadrants, raw token match) assumed the former. The framing effect argues for the latter and it was never isolated. That distinction decides the mechanism, so a mechanism proposal now would be guesswork.\n\n**ONE discriminating read-only diagnostic (CPU, no encoder, <120 s, no new held read).** Reuse the archived `inshop-bbox-context-v1` receipt (151 cropped margins already computed) plus the released garment-box file and image sizes:\n- For each miss triple, compute garment-box area fraction and box centre offset for query, positive and impostor from metadata only.\n- Predeclare: if cropped rescue is concentrated where the query\u2013positive box-scale ratio deviates most from 1 (top tercile rescue \u2265 1.5\u00d7 bottom tercile, product-bootstrap lower > 1), the loss is scale/framing normalization, and the next mechanism is a training-only scale-canonical view (box-scale-matched RandomResizedCrop *scale*, not position).
